result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers name the four problem behaviors and propose good fixes. B goes further on the save model and reset: an Undo toast, keeping thresholds in one unit internally, a specific confirmation, and splitting out 'Restore recommended alerts'. A is somewhat stronger on post-release safety with feature flags and staged rollout, but it overclaims that ordering is 'almost certainly the main cause'. B's suggestion to remove engineering knobs runs slightly against keeping every option, though B defers it to a later release. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers name all four problem behaviors, propose sensible default alerts plus copying from another hive, and regroup the 38 settings without removing any. A's save model is slightly stronger, with in-place status and Undo toasts. B wins on handling the lack of testing: it suggests feature flags or a staged rollout, lists specific metrics to watch, and flags the risks of its own suggestions, although it overclaims that the setting order is 'almost certainly' the main cause.
